passages.text: Then the men of Ephraim said to Gideon, “Why have you done this to us? Why did you fail to call us when you went to fight against Midian?” And they contended with him violently.
passages.sermon:
The men of Ephraim spoke to Gideon.
They said, "Why did you do this to us?"
They asked, "Why did you not call us?"
They said, "You went to fight against Midian."
They argued with Gideon very strongly.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ אֵלָ֜יו אִ֣ישׁ אֶפְרַ֗יִם מָֽה־ הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ עָשִׂ֣יתָ לָּ֔נוּ לְבִלְתִּי֙ קְרֹ֣אות לָ֔נוּ כִּ֥י הָלַ֖כְתָּ לְהִלָּחֵ֣ם בְּמִדְיָ֑ן וַיְרִיב֥וּן אִתּ֖וֹ בְּחָזְקָֽה׃

passages.text: But Gideon answered them, “Now what have I accomplished compared to you? Are not the gleanings of Ephraim better than the grape harvest of Abiezer?
passages.sermon:
Gideon spoke to the men of Ephraim.
He said, "What have I done now compared to you?"
You are men of Ephraim.
I am from Abiezer.
The gleanings of Ephraim are better than the full harvest of Abiezer.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם מֶה־ עָשִׂ֥יתִי עַתָּ֖ה כָּכֶ֑ם הֲל֗וֹא ט֛וֹב עֹלְל֥וֹת אֶפְרַ֖יִם מִבְצִ֥יר אֲבִיעֶֽזֶר׃

passages.text: God has delivered Oreb and Zeeb, the two princes of Midian, into your hand. What was I able to do compared to you?” When he had said this, their anger against him subsided.
passages.sermon:
God gave Oreb and Zeeb to you.
Oreb and Zeeb were princes of Midian.
You captured them.
I did not do as much as you did.
I could not do what you have done.
When Gideon said this, the men of Ephraim calmed down.
Their anger against Gideon ended.
passages.original: בְּיֶדְכֶם֩ נָתַ֨ן אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶת־ שָׂרֵ֤י מִדְיָן֙ אֶת־ עֹרֵ֣ב וְאֶת־ זְאֵ֔ב וּמַה־ יָּכֹ֖לְתִּי עֲשׂ֣וֹת כָּכֶ֑ם אָ֗ז רָפְתָ֤ה רוּחָם֙ מֵֽעָלָ֔יו בְּדַבְּר֖וֹ הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Then Gideon and his three hundred men came to the Jordan and crossed it, exhausted yet still in pursuit.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a leader and judge of Israel.
Gideon had three hundred men with him.
Gideon and his men came to the Jordan River.
They crossed the Jordan River.
Gideon and his men were very tired.
They were still chasing their enemies.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֥א גִדְע֖וֹן הַיַּרְדֵּ֑נָה עֹבֵ֣ר ה֗וּא וּשְׁלֹשׁ־ מֵא֤וֹת הָאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ עֲיֵפִ֖ים וְרֹדְפִֽים׃

passages.text: So Gideon said to the men of Succoth, “Please give my troops some bread, for they are exhausted, and I am still pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.”
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a leader and judge of Israel.
He led three hundred men against the Midianites.
Gideon and his men were very tired.
They were still chasing their enemies.
Their enemies were Zebah and Zalmunna.
Zebah and Zalmunna were kings of Midian.
Gideon spoke to the men of Succoth.
He said, “Please give bread to my men.
They are exhausted.
I am still pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לְאַנְשֵׁ֣י סֻכּ֔וֹת תְּנוּ־ נָא֙ כִּכְּר֣וֹת לֶ֔חֶם לָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּרַגְלָ֑י כִּי־ עֲיֵפִ֣ים הֵ֔ם וְאָנֹכִ֗י רֹדֵ֛ף אַחֲרֵ֛י זֶ֥בַח וְצַלְמֻנָּ֖ע מַלְכֵ֥י מִדְיָֽן׃

passages.text: But the leaders of Succoth asked, “Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your possession, that we should give bread to your army?”
passages.sermon:
The leaders of Succoth spoke to Gideon.
They asked Gideon a question.
They said, “Do you already have Zebah and Zalmunna in your hands?”
Zebah and Zalmunna were the kings of Midian.
They continued, “Should we give bread to your army now?”
They doubted Gideon’s victory.
They refused to help Gideon and his men.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ שָׂרֵ֣י סֻכּ֔וֹת הֲ֠כַף זֶ֧בַח וְצַלְמֻנָּ֛ע עַתָּ֖ה בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ כִּֽי־ נִתֵּ֥ן לִֽצְבָאֲךָ֖ לָֽחֶם׃

passages.text: “Very well,” Gideon replied, “when the LORD has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will tear your flesh with the thorns and briers of the wilderness!”
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a leader of Israel.
Gideon spoke to the leaders of Succoth.
Gideon said, "Very well."
Gideon said, "When the LORD gives Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will punish you."
Gideon said, "I will tear your flesh with the thorns and briers of the wilderness."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר גִּדְע֔וֹן לָכֵ֗ן בְּתֵ֧ת יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ זֶ֥בַח וְאֶת־ צַלְמֻנָּ֖ע בְּיָדִ֑י וְדַשְׁתִּי֙ אֶת־ בְּשַׂרְכֶ֔ם אֶת־ קוֹצֵ֥י הַמִּדְבָּ֖ר וְאֶת־ הַֽבַּרְקֳנִֽים׃

passages.text: From there he went up to Penuel and asked the same from them, but the men of Penuel gave the same response as the men of Succoth.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a leader and judge of Israel.
He left Succoth and went to Penuel.
He spoke to the people of Penuel.
He asked them for bread for his army.
The men of Penuel answered him.
They gave the same answer as the men of Succoth.
They refused to help Gideon and his men.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַל מִשָּׁם֙ פְּנוּאֵ֔ל וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם כָּזֹ֑את וַיַּעֲנ֤וּ אוֹתוֹ֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י פְנוּאֵ֔ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָנ֖וּ אַנְשֵׁ֥י סֻכּֽוֹת׃

passages.text: So Gideon told the men of Penuel, “When I return in triumph, I will tear down this tower!”
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a leader and judge of Israel.
He spoke to the men of Penuel.
He said, “When I return safely,
I will tear down this tower.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֛אמֶר גַּם־ לְאַנְשֵׁ֥י פְנוּאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר בְּשׁוּבִ֣י בְשָׁל֔וֹם אֶתֹּ֖ץ אֶת־ הַמִּגְדָּ֥ל הַזֶּֽה׃פ

passages.text: Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with their army of about fifteen thousand men—all that were left of the armies of the people of the east. A hundred and twenty thousand swordsmen had already fallen.
passages.sermon:
Zebah and Zalmunna were kings of Midian.
They were in a place called Karkor.
Their army was with them.
Their army had about fifteen thousand men.
These men were all that remained from the armies of the people of the east.
Earlier, the armies of the people of the east had many more men.
A hundred and twenty thousand swordsmen had already died.
passages.original: וְזֶ֨בַח וְצַלְמֻנָּ֜ע בַּקַּרְקֹ֗ר וּמַחֲנֵיהֶ֤ם עִמָּם֙ כַּחֲמֵ֤שֶׁת עָשָׂר֙ אֶ֔לֶף כֹּ֚ל הַנּ֣וֹתָרִ֔ים מִכֹּ֖ל מַחֲנֵ֣ה בְנֵי־ קֶ֑דֶם וְהַנֹּ֣פְלִ֔ים מֵאָ֨ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף אִ֖ישׁ שֹׁ֥לֵֽף חָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: And Gideon went up by way of the caravan route east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and he attacked their army, taking them by surprise.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a leader of Israel.
Gideon went up by the caravan route.
This route was east of Nobah and Jogbehah.
Gideon attacked the enemy army.
The enemy army felt safe and unprepared.
Gideon surprised them with his attack.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַל גִּדְע֗וֹן דֶּ֚רֶךְ הַשְּׁכוּנֵ֣י בָֽאֳהָלִ֔ים מִקֶּ֥דֶם לְנֹ֖בַח וְיָגְבֳּהָ֑ה וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וְהַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה הָ֥יָה בֶֽטַח׃

passages.text: When Zebah and Zalmunna fled, Gideon pursued and captured these two kings of Midian, routing their entire army.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a leader of Israel.
Zebah and Zalmunna were kings of Midian.
Zebah and Zalmunna fled from Gideon.
Gideon chased after Zebah and Zalmunna.
Gideon caught Zebah and Zalmunna.
Gideon captured both kings of Midian.
Gideon defeated the entire Midianite army.
Gideon caused the whole army to panic and scatter.
passages.original: וַיָּנ֗וּסוּ זֶ֚בַח וְצַלְמֻנָּ֔ע וַיִּרְדֹּ֖ף אַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּלְכֹּ֞ד אֶת־ שְׁנֵ֣י׀ מַלְכֵ֣י מִדְיָ֗ן אֶת־ זֶ֙בַח֙ וְאֶת־ צַלְמֻנָּ֔ע וְכָל־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה הֶחֱרִֽיד׃

passages.text: After this, Gideon son of Joash returned from the battle along the Ascent of Heres.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was the son of Joash.
Gideon fought in a battle.
After the battle, Gideon returned.
Gideon came back by way of the Ascent of Heres.
passages.original: וַיָּ֛שָׁב גִּדְע֥וֹן בֶּן־ יוֹאָ֖שׁ מִן־ הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה מִֽלְמַעֲלֵ֖ה הֶחָֽרֶס׃

passages.text: There he captured a young man of Succoth and interrogated him. The young man wrote down for him the names of the seventy-seven leaders and elders of Succoth.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was the son of Joash.
Gideon returned from battle.
Gideon came by the Ascent of Heres.
Gideon captured a young man from Succoth.
Gideon questioned the young man.
The young man wrote down names for Gideon.
He listed the leaders of Succoth.
He also listed the elders of Succoth.
There were seventy-seven men in total.
passages.original: וַיִּלְכָּד־ נַ֛עַר מֵאַנְשֵׁ֥י סֻכּ֖וֹת וַיִּשְׁאָלֵ֑הוּ וַיִּכְתֹּ֨ב אֵלָ֜יו אֶת־ שָׂרֵ֤י סֻכּוֹת֙ וְאֶת־ זְקֵנֶ֔יהָ שִׁבְעִ֥ים וְשִׁבְעָ֖ה אִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: And Gideon went to the men of Succoth and said, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, ‘Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your possession, that we should give bread to your weary men?’ ”
passages.sermon:
Gideon was the son of Joash.
Gideon went to the men of Succoth.
He spoke to them.
He said, "Here are Zebah and Zalmunna."
"You taunted me about them."
"You said, 'Are Zebah and Zalmunna already in your hand?'
'Why should we give bread to your weary men?'"
passages.original: וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל־ אַנְשֵׁ֣י סֻכּ֔וֹת וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֖ה זֶ֣בַח וְצַלְמֻנָּ֑ע אֲשֶׁר֩ חֵרַפְתֶּ֨ם אוֹתִ֜י לֵאמֹ֗ר הֲ֠כַף זֶ֣בַח וְצַלְמֻנָּ֤ע עַתָּה֙ בְּיָדֶ֔ךָ כִּ֥י נִתֵּ֛ן לַאֲנָשֶׁ֥יךָ הַיְּעֵפִ֖ים לָֽחֶם׃

passages.text: Then he took the elders of the city, and using the thorns and briers of the wilderness, he disciplined the men of Succoth.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a leader and judge of Israel.
He took the elders of the city of Succoth.
He gathered thorns and briers from the wilderness.
He used the thorns and briers to punish the men of Succoth.
He disciplined them as a consequence for their actions.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת־ זִקְנֵ֣י הָעִ֔יר וְאֶת־ קוֹצֵ֥י הַמִּדְבָּ֖ר וְאֶת־ הַֽבַּרְקֳנִ֑ים וַיֹּ֣דַע בָּהֶ֔ם אֵ֖ת אַנְשֵׁ֥י סֻכּֽוֹת׃

passages.text: He also pulled down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a leader and judge of Israel.
He went to the city of Penuel.
He tore down the tower in Penuel.
He killed the men of that city.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ מִגְדַּ֥ל פְּנוּאֵ֖ל נָתָ֑ץ וַֽיַּהֲרֹ֖ג אֶת־ אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעִֽיר׃

passages.text: Next, Gideon asked Zebah and Zalmunna, “What kind of men did you kill at Tabor?” “Men like you,” they answered, “each one resembling the son of a king.”
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a judge and leader of Israel.
Zebah and Zalmunna were enemy kings.
Gideon spoke to Zebah and Zalmunna.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Where are the men you killed at Tabor?”
Zebah and Zalmunna answered him.
They said, “They were men like you.”
They said, “Each one looked like a king’s son.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֶל־ זֶ֙בַח֙ וְאֶל־ צַלְמֻנָּ֔ע אֵיפֹה֙ הָאֲנָשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֲרַגְתֶּ֖ם בְּתָב֑וֹר וַֽיֹּאמרוּ֙ כָּמ֣וֹךָ כְמוֹהֶ֔ם אֶחָ֕ד כְּתֹ֖אַר בְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: “They were my brothers,” Gideon replied, “the sons of my mother! As surely as the LORD lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you.”
passages.sermon:
Gideon spoke to Zebah and Zalmunna.
He said, "They were my brothers."
He said, "They were sons of my mother."
Gideon said, "As surely as the LORD lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you."
passages.original: וַיֹּאמַ֕ר אַחַ֥י בְּנֵֽי־ אִמִּ֖י הֵ֑ם חַי־ יְהוָ֗ה ל֚וּ הַחֲיִתֶ֣ם אוֹתָ֔ם לֹ֥א הָרַ֖גְתִּי אֶתְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: So he said to Jether, his firstborn, “Get up and kill them.” But the young man did not draw his sword; he was fearful because he was still a youth.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a leader and judge of Israel.
Gideon spoke to Jether, his firstborn son.
Gideon said, “Get up and kill them.”
Jether was a young man.
Jether did not draw his sword.
Jether was afraid.
Jether was still a youth.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לְיֶ֣תֶר בְּכוֹר֔וֹ ק֖וּם הֲרֹ֣ג אוֹתָ֑ם וְלֹא־ שָׁלַ֨ף הַנַּ֤עַר חַרְבּוֹ֙ כִּ֣י יָרֵ֔א כִּ֥י עוֹדֶ֖נּוּ נָֽעַר׃

passages.text: Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, “Get up and kill us yourself, for as the man is, so is his strength.” So Gideon got up and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and he took the crescent ornaments from the necks of their camels.
passages.sermon:
Zebah and Zalmunna were two enemy kings.
They spoke to Gideon.
They said, “Get up and kill us yourself.”
They said, “A man’s strength shows who he is.”
Gideon got up.
Gideon killed Zebah and Zalmunna.
Gideon took the crescent ornaments.
These ornaments were on the necks of their camels.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֜אמֶר זֶ֣בַח וְצַלְמֻנָּ֗ע ק֤וּם אַתָּה֙ וּפְגַע־ בָּ֔נוּ כִּ֥י כָאִ֖ישׁ גְּבוּרָת֑וֹ וַיָּ֣קָם גִּדְע֗וֹן וַֽיַּהֲרֹג֙ אֶת־ זֶ֣בַח וְאֶת־ צַלְמֻנָּ֔ע וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת־ הַשַּׂ֣הֲרֹנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּצַוְּארֵ֥י גְמַלֵּיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then the Israelites said to Gideon, “Rule over us—you and your son and grandson—for you have saved us from the hand of Midian.”
passages.sermon:
The Israelites spoke to Gideon.
They said, “Rule over us.”
They wanted Gideon to be their leader.
They also wanted his son to rule after him.
They wanted his grandson to rule after his son.
They said, “You saved us from the hand of Midian.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ אִֽישׁ־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־ גִּדְע֔וֹן מְשָׁל־ בָּ֙נוּ֙ גַּם־ אַתָּ֔ה גַּם־ בִּנְךָ֖ גַּ֣ם בֶּן־ בְּנֶ֑ךָ כִּ֥י הוֹשַׁעְתָּ֖נוּ מִיַּ֥ד מִדְיָֽן׃

passages.text: But Gideon replied, “I will not rule over you, nor will my son. The LORD shall rule over you.”
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a leader of Israel.
\r\nThe Israelites asked Gideon to rule over them.
\r\nGideon answered the Israelites.
\r\nGideon said, "I will not rule over you."
\r\nGideon said, "My son will not rule over you."
\r\nGideon said, "The LORD will rule over you."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ גִּדְע֔וֹן לֹֽא־ אֶמְשֹׁ֤ל אֲנִי֙ בָּכֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא־ יִמְשֹׁ֥ל בְּנִ֖י בָּכֶ֑ם יְהוָ֖ה יִמְשֹׁ֥ל בָּכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then he added, “Let me make a request of you, that each of you give me an earring from his plunder.” (For the enemies had gold earrings because they were Ishmaelites.)
passages.sermon:
Gideon spoke to the Israelites.
He said, "I have a request."
"Each man, give me an earring from your share of the plunder."
The enemies wore gold earrings.
The enemies were Ishmaelites.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם גִּדְע֗וֹן אֶשְׁאֲלָ֤ה מִכֶּם֙ שְׁאֵלָ֔ה וּתְנוּ־ לִ֕י אִ֖ישׁ נֶ֣זֶם שְׁלָל֑וֹ כִּֽי־ נִזְמֵ֤י זָהָב֙ לָהֶ֔ם כִּ֥י יִשְׁמְעֵאלִ֖ים הֵֽם׃

passages.text: “We will give them gladly,” they replied. So they spread out a garment, and each man threw an earring from his plunder onto it.
passages.sermon:
The people answered Gideon.
They said, “We will give the earrings.”
They spread out a garment on the ground.
Each man took an earring from his plunder.
Each man threw his earring onto the garment.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ נָת֣וֹן נִתֵּ֑ן וַֽיִּפְרְשׂוּ֙ אֶת־ הַשִּׂמְלָ֔ה וַיַּשְׁלִ֣יכוּ שָׁ֔מָּה אִ֖ישׁ נֶ֥זֶם שְׁלָלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The weight of the gold earrings he had requested was 1,700 shekels, in addition to the crescent ornaments, the pendants, the purple garments of the kings of Midian, and the chains from the necks of their camels.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a leader of Israel.
He asked the people for gold earrings from their plunder.
The people gave him the earrings.
The gold earrings weighed 1,700 shekels.
This weight did not include other items.
There were crescent ornaments.
There were pendants.
There were purple garments that belonged to the kings of Midian.
There were chains from the necks of their camels.
Gideon received all these things in addition to the gold earrings.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י מִשְׁקַ֞ל נִזְמֵ֤י הַזָּהָב֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁאָ֔ל אֶ֥לֶף וּשְׁבַע־ מֵא֖וֹת זָהָ֑ב לְ֠בַד מִן־ הַשַּׂהֲרֹנִ֨ים וְהַנְּטִפ֜וֹת וּבִגְדֵ֣י הָאַרְגָּמָ֗ן שֶׁעַל֙ מַלְכֵ֣י מִדְיָ֔ן וּלְבַד֙ מִן־ הָ֣עֲנָק֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּצַוְּארֵ֥י גְמַלֵּיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: From all this Gideon made an ephod, which he placed in Ophrah, his hometown. But soon all Israel prostituted themselves by worshiping it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his household.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a leader of Israel.
Gideon took the gold and other items.
Gideon made an ephod from them.
An ephod is a special garment or object used in worship.
Gideon placed the ephod in Ophrah.
Ophrah was Gideon's hometown.
All Israel began to worship the ephod there.
The people turned away from God and worshiped the ephod.
This became a trap for Gideon and his family.
passages.original: וַיַּעַשׂ֩ אוֹת֨וֹ גִדְע֜וֹן לְאֵפ֗וֹד וַיַּצֵּ֨ג אוֹת֤וֹ בְעִירוֹ֙ בְּעָפְרָ֔ה וַיִּזְנ֧וּ כָֽל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אַחֲרָ֖יו שָׁ֑ם וַיְהִ֛י לְגִדְע֥וֹן וּלְבֵית֖וֹ לְמוֹקֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: In this way Midian was subdued before the Israelites and did not raise its head again. So the land had rest for forty years in the days of Gideon, and he—Jerubbaal son of Joash—returned home and settled down.
passages.sermon:
Midian was an enemy nation.
The Israelites defeated Midian.
Midian became weak before the Israelites.
Midian did not become strong again.
The land became peaceful.
The land had rest for forty years.
This happened during the days of Gideon.
Gideon was also called Jerubbaal.
Gideon was the son of Joash.
Gideon returned to his home.
Gideon lived in his house.
passages.original: וַיִּכָּנַ֣ע מִדְיָ֗ן לִפְנֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלֹ֥א יָסְפ֖וּ לָשֵׂ֣את רֹאשָׁ֑ם וַתִּשְׁקֹ֥ט הָאָ֛רֶץ אַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה בִּימֵ֥י גִדְעֽוֹן׃פ וַיֵּ֛לֶךְ יְרֻבַּ֥עַל בֶּן־ יוֹאָ֖שׁ וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בְּבֵיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Gideon had seventy sons of his own, since he had many wives.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a leader of Israel.
Gideon had many wives.
Gideon became the father of seventy sons.
All these sons were his own children.
passages.original: וּלְגִדְע֗וֹן הָיוּ֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים בָּנִ֔ים יֹצְאֵ֖י יְרֵכ֑וֹ כִּֽי־ נָשִׁ֥ים רַבּ֖וֹת הָ֥יוּ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: His concubine, who dwelt in Shechem, also bore him a son, and he named him Abimelech.
passages.sermon:
Gideon had a concubine.
She lived in Shechem.
She bore Gideon a son.
Gideon named his son Abimelech.
passages.original: וּפִֽילַגְשׁוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּשְׁכֶ֔ם יָֽלְדָה־ לּ֥וֹ גַם־ הִ֖יא בֵּ֑ן וַיָּ֥שֶׂם אֶת־ שְׁמ֖וֹ אֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: Later, Gideon son of Joash died at a ripe old age and was buried in the tomb of his father Joash in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was the son of Joash.
Gideon lived to a ripe old age.
Gideon died.
People buried Gideon in the tomb of his father Joash.
This tomb was in Ophrah.
Ophrah belonged to the Abiezrites.
passages.original: וַיָּ֛מָת גִּדְע֥וֹן בֶּן־ יוֹאָ֖שׁ בְּשֵׂיבָ֣ה טוֹבָ֑ה וַיִּקָּבֵ֗ר בְּקֶ֙בֶר֙ יוֹאָ֣שׁ אָבִ֔יו בְּעָפְרָ֖ה אֲבִ֥י הָֽעֶזְרִֽי׃פ

passages.text: And as soon as Gideon was dead, the Israelites turned and prostituted themselves with the Baals, and they set up Baal-berith as their god.
passages.sermon:
Gideon was a leader of Israel.
Gideon died.
After Gideon died, the Israelites changed their ways.
The Israelites turned away from God.
The Israelites worshiped the Baals.
The Israelites chose Baal-berith to be their god.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ מֵ֣ת גִּדְע֔וֹן וַיָּשׁ֙וּבוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּזְנ֖וּ אַחֲרֵ֣י הַבְּעָלִ֑ים וַיָּשִׂ֧ימוּ לָהֶ֛ם בַּ֥עַל בְּרִ֖ית לֵאלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: The Israelites failed to remember the LORD their God who had delivered them from the hands of all their enemies on every side.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites did not remember the LORD.
The LORD is their God.
The LORD saved the Israelites.
He rescued them from all their enemies.
Their enemies surrounded them on every side.
passages.original: וְלֹ֤א זָֽכְרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם הַמַּצִּ֥יל אוֹתָ֛ם מִיַּ֥ד כָּל־ אֹיְבֵיהֶ֖ם מִסָּבִֽיב׃

passages.text: They did not show kindness to the house of Jerubbaal (that is, Gideon) for all the good things he had done for Israel.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites did not show kindness to the family of Jerubbaal.
Jerubbaal is Gideon.
Gideon had done many good things for Israel.
The Israelites did not repay his family for all the good he had done.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ עָשׂ֣וּ חֶ֔סֶד עִם־ בֵּ֥ית יְרֻבַּ֖עַל גִּדְע֑וֹן כְּכָל־ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה עִם־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
